item.title: Re: I made an audio adaptation of this !
item.content:encoded:
Sorry for not noticing this earlier, but you totally did this justice. I'm at work, grinning like a fool, and I can't really tell them why without looking like a crazy person.

Character-Bibs is generally me with some degree of badassitude, so I wasn't expecting the southern-ish drawl, but it really worked well. Plus, it stands to reason, since I do a lot of Ain'ts and Yalls. An excellent combo of seriousness and digression, which is the cornerstone of the character as I write it. The only thing that's different from this and my vision is that Bibs talks fast. Very fast. But really, that's a quibble, and if people listen to this and use it as a template for reading any of my stuff, I'm proud.

Double-kudos has to be given for perfectly capturing the moment near the end when Bibs 'dropped character' and ranted about Bill.

Beautiful. Absolutely beautiful.

This was posted a few days ago and I didn't notice it, so sorry for the delay in responding.

In my mind, Bibs's name-tats aren't anywhere actively visible (high upper arm, and Bibs was pulling his shirt down to show everyone). They don't pose a problem when he's going into GOC / MC&D facilities, because like Bland says, he's a known Foundation Agent.

When Bibs goes into one of those facilities, he's not going in the front door. Either he's going in dead silent (meaning some way that nobody knows he's in there at all), or he's posing as a service worker and relying on the fact that 'important people' in large buildings ignore service workers.

item.content:encoded:
Yoric, I could kiss you.

The comments about badassery threw me for a loop. In my own mind, I was writing that Bibs is trying too hard. From people he respects, Bibs brushes off compliments about his skills / job / etc. He doesn't let himself even think he's a badass. It's only when he's briefing newbies does he let himself act like an arrogant, I know-everything-down-to-the-second kind of guy.

Bibs isn't a badass… and he doesn't even want to be seen as one.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Long and short of this one? I had read Clef's Guide To Reality Warpers, and was writing one about training / briefing Agents. Then Orientation was written, and rather than throw away the work, I decided to write it a primer for Agents who do initial intelligence and appraisal of items. My goal of the piece was to treat Intel Agents somewhat as know-it-alls, because knowing stuff is their job.

I'm not 100% sure if the title is appropriate, but it came out of an unintended accident. I tend to write like I talk, and when I was going over the piece I realized that I was writing the word "shit" to cover things like intelligence, recon, etc. Rather than change a few of them, I decided to keep them in, mentally fanwank that Character-Bibs uses the term as a vague "important information" word, and labelled the page accordingly.
